guide.soulcatcherplus.name: Soul Catcher's Notes
guide.soulcatcherplus.landing: Death leaves a trace that few can see. A scythe holds it, a cage gathers its energy, and a bestiary remembers the creatures you have caught.
guide.soulcatcherplus.subtitle: Soul Catcher Plus

guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.capture.pag: Begin with simple equipment and your first soul. A good catcher learns to care for companions as well as summon them.
To catch a soul, you will need a scythe and a soul cage. Keep the cage in your offhand or on your hotbar.
Switch the scythe to Harvest mode and use it on a creature — right mouse button by default. A mark will appear. It fades quickly: defeat the creature before the bond breaks.
A glowing soul will remain after your victory. Use the scythe on it to preserve the captured form in your bestiary. Only you can claim a soul bearing your mark.
Do not linger: an unattended trace will soon fade away.
guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.energy.name: Soul energy
guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.energy.page: Victories fill your cages with energy. Both you and your summoned companions can gather it.$(br2)This power sustains a summon. The mightier the creature, the more energy it takes to bring it back into the world.
A captured form remains in your bestiary. Once a bond is made, you can call upon that soul again, as long as you have the strength to summon it.
Hold a scythe in either hand and open the bestiary with its assigned key — O by default.$(br2)Choose a captured soul and summon it. Make sure your party has room and your cage holds enough energy.
Different creature forms can be found and preserved separately. Especially mighty souls are marked in purple.
Mark your favorite companions with a star to find them more easily. Here you can also choose the tint of their spectral forms or release an unwanted soul forever.
guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.orders.name: Orders
guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.orders.page: With a scythe in hand, hold the command wheel key — R by default. Point at a companion, then at an order, and release the key.
Returning the pointer to the center clears your choice. All creatures lets you address the entire party.
$(thing)Follow$() — accompany you, defend you and help against those you strike. A companion that strays too far will leave the fight to return.
$(thing)Aggressive$() — follow you and seek nearby hostile creatures. Once fighting, the soul keeps its chosen enemy instead of following your every step.
Only when you are beyond teleport range will it abandon the fight and try to return. Without a target, it follows normally.

$(thing)Wait$() — stay in place and stop fighting.$(br2)$(thing)Guard$() — defend the place where you stood when giving the order. The companion watches for nearby monsters and pursues them around that post.
$(thing)Teleport$() — bring a companion close, keeping its health and orders. A guard takes up a new post beside you.
$(thing)Recall$() — end the summon without losing the captured form. Part of the companion's remaining strength returns as soul energy to your cages.
$(thing)Attack a target$() — switch the scythe to Command mode and use it on an enemy — right mouse button by default. The addressed companions take that target and switch to Follow.
The other orders are also available in the bestiary — O by default.
guide.soulcatcherplus.basics.lifecycle.p: The death of a spectral body does not destroy its bond. The soul will need time to recover before answering your call again.
You can recall a companion before that happens, returning some energy to your cages. Leave room for it: any excess power will disperse.
If a companion is delayed on the road, use the Teleport order.
A scythe is both a weapon and a bond with your party. A finer tool lets you lead more companions.
Begin with an iron scythe. In time, diamond and netherite may take its place. A netherite scythe requires a smithing table and a diamond base.
The supreme scythe is made from bones and a Nether Star. It is a tool for a catcher ready to gather a powerful party.
Scythes accept sword enchantments. Do not neglect these charms when seeking dangerous prey.
guide.soulcatcherplus.equipment.cages.pa: The blue light inside a cage reveals the energy held within. A finer vessel can hold a greater reserve.
An iron cage will serve you at first. Diamond and netherite will prepare you for more demanding summons. The supreme cage is made from bones and a Nether Star.
Summoning uses the cage in your offhand. If there is none, it uses the leftmost cage on your hotbar.
The energy for a single summon must be held in one cage. When gathering your spoils, a full vessel passes the excess to the next available cages.
guide.soulcatcherplus.equipment.guide.pa: If these notes are lost, combine an ordinary book with soul sand.$(br2)May the new book serve you on your travels — or reach someone just beginning to hear the souls.
guide.soulcatcherplus.enchantments.harve: An enchanted scythe helps draw more energy from your victories.$(br2)Keep it in your hand when going into battle, and your cage will fill more generously.
guide.soulcatcherplus.enchantments.capac: These charms let a cage hold more energy.$(br2)They are especially useful to a catcher who travels far from home and prepares a reserve for the summons ahead.
guide.soulcatcherplus.enchantments.slots: These charms are woven into armor to strengthen the bond between a catcher and their companions.
Wearing enchanted armor lets you sustain a larger party. A good scythe alone may not be enough for someone who wishes to lead many.
Some souls have survived in old scrolls. Before breaking a seal, read which creature is bound to it.
Take the scroll in hand and use it. The seal will break, and the form held within will appear in your bestiary. You will still need energy and room in your party to summon it.
Scrolls of Forgotten Souls are occasionally found in chests. Their companions are reached through surviving seals, rather than caught with a scythe.
guide.soulcatcherplus.forgotten.raven.pa: A small raven rests on its owner’s shoulder and watches for nearby spoils.

It seeks items and souls that you can claim, gathers several finds and brings them back. If your inventory is full, the spoils will be left at your feet.$(br2)You will need a cage to receive the souls it brings.
The raven is no fighter. Take care of your collector.
A little skeleton carries an Ender Chest much heavier than itself. Use the courier to reach your storage far from home.$(br2)Other travelers can call upon it too. Each will see their own belongings.
The courier waits patiently while its chest is open. Even if its summon ends, the contents of your storage will remain safe.
guide.soulcatcherplus.forgotten.shaman.p: The shaman accompanies your party with a staff and an amulet. Its rites strengthen you and your allied souls, helping them fight and recover from wounds.$(br2)Stay nearby to keep its aid close at hand.
The shaman itself avoids combat. See to its protection, and it will care for those you lead.
guide.soulcatcherplus.commands.energy.pa: $(thing)/soulcatcher energy <amount>$()$(br2)Sets the energy stored in your active cage. It replaces the current amount rather than adding to it.
Keep a cage in your offhand or hotbar. The offhand takes priority; otherwise the leftmost hotbar cage is used.
The input range is 0 to 1000000. The stored amount is capped at the cage’s actual capacity. Zero empties it.
This command acts on the player running it.$(br2)From the server console, run it as a player:$(br)/execute as Steve run soulcatcher energy 500
guide.soulcatcherplus.commands.scroll.pa: $(thing)/soulcatcher scroll <mob> [player]$()$(br2)Gives one scroll containing the default form of that mob. Use the scroll to add its soul to the bestiary.
Without a recipient, the scroll goes to you. From the console, specify a player name or a selector for one player.
Use an entity ID from Minecraft or an installed mod. Use Tab (default) to complete IDs and recipients.$(br2)Examples:$(br)/soulcatcher scroll minecraft:creeper

The namespace@mob form is also accepted:$(br)minecraft@creeper$(br2)The command chooses a normal, boss or Forgotten Soul scroll automatically. If the recipient has no room for it, free inventory space and try again.
The ID must refer to a mob, not an item or projectile.
